thread:
elaine-sales: FYI Pinecrest POC reporting very slow first-token times this morning — some requests are 2.5s TTFT. They're on a 16k context, using rwd-open-13b-q4 and default batching/prefill settings. Can we swarm?

pinecrest-admin: Confirmed. We also saw a spike in 429s around 10:12 UTC. No config changes on our side.

sam-se: Thanks. Can you paste the SDK request snippet and the model config? Also, are they using prefill/prefill_policy?

pinecrest-admin: SDK call looks like: `client.generate({model: "rwd-open-13b-q4", input: prompt, max_tokens: 512, stream: false})` — no explicit prefill.

mike-eng: Two quick suspects: (1) batching window causing head-of-line delays, (2) KV cache cold misses because no prefill/warmup. Any cache-miss metrics?

pinecrest-admin: Cache miss ratio reported by runtime: `kv_cache_miss: 0.93` and `avg_batch_wait_ms: 320`.

sam-se: That avg_batch_wait_ms is the problem. Their client is queuing small requests and our batching window is aggregating into bigger batches with higher head latency. Can they set batch_size/latency hints in the route?

elaine-sales: They asked about pricing impact if we enable prefill/warmup — will that bill as normal tokens?

junior-support: Yes — prefill/warmup is normal token usage (hosted usage-based billing). We can recommend a short warmup policy with a small warmup token budget to reduce TTFT without big cost.

mike-eng: Ops steps: (A) try enabling `prefill_policy: "light"` for their route, (B) lower per-request batch_max_tokens or set `latency_slo_ms: 200` so runtime prefers smaller batches, (C) enable KV prefetch for common prompts.

pinecrest-admin: Quick test results after enabling `latency_slo_ms:200` — TTFT dropped to ~450ms for single-turn requests. But for long context (>8k) TTFT still ~1.2s.

sam-se: That's expected — large sequence lengths force kernel selection that increases per-token prep. For large contexts, prefetching KV slices helps. We should push a step-by-step configuration for them.

mike-eng: Also saw these lines in the edge logs at 10:12: `ERROR rate_limiter.go:92: request_rejected: route_concurrency_limit` and `WARN runtime_prefetch.go:47: kv_cache_stale:true` — route concurrency cap plus stale cache explains the 429 + slow TTFT combo.

ops-bot: Deployment autoscaler triggered scale-up: added 2 x p4d workers to pool at 10:18 UTC.

pinecrest-admin: After scale-up, throughput much better, but still occasional 429s during bursted test. They use parallel 20 concurrent requests in preflight.

sam-se: For parallel bursts, recommend burst_capacity or reserved dedicated capacity. We can also stagger client parallelism or use client-side jitter.

junior-support: Pricing note: burst_capacity on Dedicated comes with monthly commitment tiers. For Hosted, short-term bursts will just be billed as usage but may hit route concurrency limits.

elaine-sales: Security Q from their legal: does prefill/warmup touch customer KMS keys? They want to make sure no plaintext context leaves their VPC for Private deployments.

mike-eng: For Private (VPC) deployments, KMS stays customer-controlled. For Hosted, customers can use our KMS integrations but plaintext does transit our control plane briefly for service. I'll draft an answer for the security questionnaire section.

pinecrest-admin: Appreciate that. Next steps we did on our side: enabled latency_slo, turned on light prefill, ran 5m burst tests, attached logs. TTFT baseline improved but we still need guidance for sustained 20qps bursts.

sam-se: Action items — (1) eng to validate route concurrency and suggest a safe concurrency limit + burst policy, (2) docs: short presales note on prefill token billing, (3) solutions: propose Dedicated reservation for sustained bursts; include ballpark commit pricing.

mike-eng: I'll open a short runbook: `steps-to-troubleshoot-ttft` — includes log grep commands: `grep "request_rejected|kv_cache_stale|avg_batch_wait_ms" /var/log/runtime/*.log` and a quick profiling curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/debug/route-metrics?route=pinecrest"`

junior-support: I'll reply to pricing + security thread in GH with the short answers and links to the KMS and Dedicated pricing pages.

elaine-sales: Thanks team. Pinecrest is asking for a short meeting at 14:00 UTC to review Dedicated vs hosted tweaks. Can someone from eng be on the call?

mike-eng: I can join the 14:00 UTC call. I'll bring the runbook and sample config.

pinecrest-admin: Good — we'll be ready with their security questionnaire items and a 10-min perf repro.

elaine-sales: Great. I'll schedule and send calendar invite. :thumbsup:

mike-eng: Final quick tip for the call: collect a small representative prompt set (5-10 prompts) and the exact concurrency pattern so we can reproduce.

pinecrest-admin: Sending prompt set and test script now in separate message.

elaine-sales: Closing the loop after the call — will post a short postmortem with what config changes we landed.
